posts.text:
1. Don't make decisions based on benchmarks.  They have too many flaws. 

2. Use your own evals 

3. If you must use benchmarks, look at the data.  Looking at just one failed task is often enough to uncover major issues.  TBH, you'll be convinced not to trust benchmarks if you do
posts.author: Hamel Husain

quoted.text:
Looking at the decision index benchmarks and wow pervasive overfitting of models!!! 

I'm more likely to use a model that has a high & consistent public + private score vs. those with a huge drift

Also, beware - the models are sorted by public scores in the individual benchmark

posts.text:
I'm not blaming anyone fwiw.  The noise can come from a variety of places, maybe:

- The model has memorized the benchmark
- The benchmark is saturated b/c models are better now
- The benchmark has tasks, graders, envs that have issues
- etc. 

Bottom line: stay skeptical
